evals.prompt: From the boba repository root, inspect the current OrderCompleted v2 contract, Orders outbox producer and affected consumers. Plan a new completion wire version carrying per-line product-name snapshots while preserving supported v2 behavior. Explain the subscriber rollout and compatibility tests. Do not edit files, publish messages or run the application.
evals.expected_output: An owner-by-owner rollout plan leaving strict v2 unchanged and introducing a separate new wire schema/version. It distinguishes legacy v1 parseability from its unsupported completion effects, preserves self-contained completion data and independent Inventory/Finance/Customers effects, and identifies old/new/invalid/unsupported payload tests. It preserves atomic domain/outbox and effect/receipt commits and stable semantic operation IDs on retry, with no consumer lookup into Orders or invented compatibility defaults.

evals.prompt: Read tests/integration/events.test.ts and the relevant producer/consumer code from the repository root. Plan verification for duplicate completion delivery and a retained Inventory recipe failure followed by owner retry. Use the existing two-tea fixture to specify exact stock, ledger and customer deltas. Do not run RabbitMQ, change stock or retry the live demo.
evals.expected_output: An evidence plan using real RabbitMQ delivery and owner APIs in isolated fixtures, retaining the original operation ID and payload on redelivery/retry. For the existing two-tea fixture it specifies stock -100 units, exactly one simulated USD sale of 1100 minor units, customer count +1 and USD spend +1100 once. It distinguishes published outbox facts from consumer success, retains visible failure until repair, retries only the owning failed effect and states that the proposed checks were not executed.

evals.prompt: Someone proposes retrying a failed completion with the same operationId but corrected quantities and says ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes it safe. Inspect the boba contracts and messaging/effect code from the repository root. Assess the claim and plan explicit conflict behavior and tests without changing code or sending messages.
evals.expected_output: A code-backed assessment that semantic deduplication alone does not compare or authorize changed payloads under a reused operation ID. It preserves the original payload/identity for ordinary retries, separates intentional correction from redelivery, calls for explicit conflicting-ID/payload behavior and public-behavior tests, and maintains atomic effect/receipt commits. It reports actual current behavior and unresolved design decisions rather than claiming conflict detection already exists.
